authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: LiveWire Group, Inc., the Company's LiveWire segment entity, disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. The Company says it does not plan to fund LiveWire beyond the existing Term Loan.
LiveWire withdrew its 2026 guidance, and the Company in turn withdrew its own LiveWire guidance.
The Company raised its 2026 outlook for wholesale shipments and worldwide dealer retail sales, and raised HDMC and HDFS guidance.

business_model.claim: The company reports three segments: Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC, motorcycles and related products), LiveWire (electric motorcycles) and Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS).
quotes: The Company has three reportable segments: Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC), LiveWire, and Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS).

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K segment revenue table
business_model.claim: HDMC is by far the largest revenue source. Segment revenue for 2025 (table in thousands) was HDMC $3,578,308, LiveWire 25,671 and HDFS 869,196, totalling $4,473,175.

HDMC sells motorcycles plus parts, accessories, apparel and trademark licences. Motorcycles were 74.3% of HDMC revenue in 2025, parts and accessories were 17.2 (percent), and apparel, licensing and other made up the rest.
quotes: HDMC also sells motorcycle parts, accessories, and apparel as well as licenses its trademarks.

business_model.basis: stated for dealer sales and the wholesale model; the revenue-recognition link is inferred
business_model.claim: HDMC sells mainly at wholesale to independent dealers and, in some overseas markets, independent distributors. These in turn sell to retail riders, and the network had 1,174 dealership points.
quotes: HDMC's products are sold to retail customers primarily through a network of independent dealers.
The Company primarily sells its products at wholesale and must rely to a large extent on a network of independent dealers and distributors to manage the retail distribution of its products.

business_model.claim: Demand is concentrated in the U.S. and Europe: about 79% of 2025 dealer retail sales of new motorcycles were in the U.S. and European 601+cc markets.
quotes: In 2025, approximately 79% of the total annual dealer retail sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles were sold in the U.S. and European 601+cc markets.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K and 10-Q management discussion
business_model.claim: HDFS provides financing around the motorcycle business and now runs a capital-light model. It sold most of its existing retail finance receivables to two counterparties, sells a portion of new originations to them, and earns servicing fees on loans it services.
quotes: HDFS earns loan servicing fees over the period it services loans purchased by the counterparties at a rate of 1% per annum for prime loans and 2.5% per annum for subprime loans.

business_model.basis: stated in the statements and the 10-Q management discussion; the one-time characterisation is stated in P5
business_model.claim: The HDFS shift sharply cut financial services revenue and operating income. Quarterly revenue fell from 261,188 to 110,758 and operating income from 438,820 to 10,758. Nine-month revenue fell from 763,587 to 339,745 (tables in thousands).
quotes: The decrease was also driven by lower interest income resulting from a smaller finance receivables portfolio, partially offset by lower interest expense and increased income from servicing fees.

business_model.claim: In the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands), motorcycles and related products brought in 3,145,861 against 3,213,431 a year earlier, financial services 339,745 against 763,587, and total revenue was 3,485,606 against 3,977,018.

HDMC's main costs are cost of goods sold and selling, administrative and engineering expense. For the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands), cost of goods sold was 2,304,903 against 2,320,261 and selling, administrative and engineering expense was 890,672 against 849,098.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release bridge table; the millions scale is inferred because the table heading is not shown
business_model.claim: HDMC gross profit is driven by volume, price and incentives, shipment mix, currency, raw materials and manufacturing costs. Quarterly gross profit went from $283 to $271 (table in millions, inferred from the row values): volume (24), price and sales incentives (12) and shipment mix (22) hurt, while manufacturing and other costs added 44.
quotes: •Third quarter gross margin percentage increased by 173 bps YoY to 28.1 percent.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release; the revenue mechanism is inferred
business_model.claim: Revenue follows motorcycle volume, and the company currently ships below retail to cut dealer inventory. Quarterly worldwide shipments were 33,616, down 8 percent, while worldwide retail sales were 35,833 against 33,984 and global dealer inventory was down 26 percent.
quotes: •HDMC global motorcycle shipments of 33,616 units in the quarter were down 8 percent vs. prior year to drive long-term dealer health and in alignment with the Back to the Bricks strategy.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K; the discretionary framing is the company's own description of the demand environment
business_model.claim: Demand is cyclical and discretionary. Worldwide dealer retail unit sales fell 12.4% in 2025, from 151,229 to 132,535, amid high interest rates and weak consumer sentiment, and retail sales track riding seasons.
quotes: Worldwide dealer retail unit sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles decreased 12.4% in 2025 compared to 2024.
Retail sales generally track closely with regional riding seasons.

business_model.claim: Tariffs are a significant cost driver. The gross cost of new or increased tariffs was about $94 million in the first nine months of 2026 against $45 million a year earlier.
quotes: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the total gross cost of new or increased tariffs implemented in 2025 and 2026 that the Company incurred was approximately $94 million, an increase from $45 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in the cash flow statement and the 10-K for the funding mix and rate effect; the margin mechanism is partly inferred
business_model.claim: HDFS funding cost is a key driver of finance earnings. HDFS funds itself with notes, asset-backed commercial paper, deposits and other debt, and in the first nine months of 2026 it repaid 810,950 of medium-term notes and borrowed 260,250 of asset-backed commercial paper (table in thousands).
quotes: a higher cost of funds that is only partially offset by increased interest rates on financing products sold by HDFS

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, earnings release and 10-Q
business_model.claim: LiveWire sells electric motorcycles and balance bikes. It is a small, loss-making segment, with 22,094 of revenue and an operating loss of (53,350) in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands). LiveWire Group disclosed going-concern doubt.
quotes: In the fourth quarter of 2026, LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its operating income/(loss) guidance.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q as management expectations
business_model.claim: Management's Back to the Bricks plan targets a cost reduction of at least $150 million plus a further $75 million of HDMC profit benefit from cost leverage and other activities, for a combined $225 million of annual benefit, to be fully realised by the end of 2027.
quotes: The Company expects these cost reduction actions to reduce its costs by at least $150 million compared to its 2025 cost base.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (registration table and footnote)
competitive_position.claim: Harley-Davidson lost share of new large-displacement motorcycle registrations in both main markets in 2025: U.S. share fell to 34.5% from 37.3% in 2024, and Europe fell to 3.4% from 5.0%.
Worldwide retail sales of new motorcycles fell 12.4% in 2025, which the company attributes to a weak macro environment and a prior-year Touring launch benefit.
quotes: Worldwide retail sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles decreased 12.4% during 2025 compared to 2024 driven primarily by declines in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific.

competitive_position.claim: Retail momentum improved in 2026. Worldwide retail sales rose 5.4% in Q3 2026 year over year, led by North America at 9.1%, while Europe fell 5.3%.
quotes: Worldwide retail sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles in the third quarter of 2026 increased 5.4% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
Retail sales were up 9.1% in North America and 0.7% in Asia Pacific, partially offset by a 5.3% decline in Europe.

competitive_position.claim: Global dealer inventory of new motorcycles ended Q3 2026 down 26 percent year over year. The company says it is aligning wholesale shipments with retail demand, which supports dealer health but held back shipments.
quotes: Global dealer inventory of new motorcycles ended Q3 2026 down 26 percent vs. Q3 2025, and down 6 percent vs Q2 2026.
HDMC global motorcycle shipments of 33,616 units in the quarter were down 8 percent vs. prior year to drive long-term dealer health and in alignment with the Back to the Bricks strategy.

competitive_position.claim: HDMC margins are mixed. Q3 gross margin rose to 28.1 percent, but HDMC operating income fell 18 percent in Q3 on lower shipments, less beneficial product mix and pricing, and restructuring charges.
quotes: Third quarter gross margin percentage increased by 173 bps YoY to 28.1 percent.
HDMC operating income was $44 million in Q3 2026, down 18 percent YoY.

The decrease in operating income from the HDMC segment for the third quarter of 2026 was driven primarily by lower motorcycle shipments, less beneficial product mix and pricing, and restructuring charges, partially offset by lower manufacturing costs, lower operating expenses and favorable currency impacts.

competitive_position.claim: Over nine months, HDMC operating income was 135,561 against 231,707 a year earlier (table in thousands), so the motorcycle business earned less than in 2025 despite the Q3 gross margin gain.
quotes: Operating income from HDMC | 44,298 | 54,119 | 135,561 | 231,707

competitive_position.claim: The company's stated competitive advantages are premium styling and customization, brand heritage, financing through HDFS, and a global dealer network. The 10-K says its motorcycles generally carry a premium price.
quotes: Harley-Davidson motorcycles offer unique styling, customization, innovative design, distinctive sound, superior quality and reliability and include a warranty.

HDMC also considers the availability of its line of motorcycle parts and accessories and apparel, the availability of financing through HDFS and its global network of dealers to be competitive advantages.

competitive_position.claim: The company relies on independent dealers (1,174 dealership points at end-2025, 554 in the U.S.) to reach retail customers. This is a dependency and a threat if dealers become unprofitable.
quotes: The Company primarily sells its products at wholesale and must rely to a large extent on a network of independent dealers and distributors to manage the retail distribution of its products.

competitive_position.claim: Price competition is a named threat. The company's motorcycles are generally priced above competitors', and a shift toward price-sensitivity would disadvantage it.
quotes: If price becomes a more important factor for consumers in the markets in which the Company competes, the Company may be at a competitive disadvantage.

competitive_position.claim: Tariffs are a growing cost pressure. Gross tariff cost for the first nine months of 2026 was about $94 million against $45 million a year earlier, and the full-year 2026 gross estimate was raised to $105 million to $120 million.
quotes: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the total gross cost of new or increased tariffs implemented in 2025 and 2026 that the Company incurred was approximately $94 million, an increase from $45 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: The new Back to the Bricks plan targets cost reductions of at least $150 million plus at least $75 million more for HDMC, for a total annual benefit of at least $225 million. It also relies on new products (Sprint, Sportster return) and targets for HDMC gross margin of 25% to 30% and operating expense below 20% of HDMC revenue.
quotes: In addition to these savings, the Company has set a target to achieve at least an additional $75 million benefit to HDMC profitability during the same time period through improved cost leverage and other activities that would result in a total annual benefit of at least $225 million.
targets HDMC operating expense as a percent of HDMC revenue to be below 20% in the medium term

competitive_position.claim: The financial services arm no longer gives the company a financing-income edge at its prior scale. After selling most retail receivables, HDFS Q3 2026 operating income was $10.8 million, down $428.1 million year over year, and HDFS faces competition from banks with cheaper capital.
quotes: Operating income from the HDFS segment in the third quarter of 2026 was $10.8 million, down $428.1 million compared to the prior year quarter.

In addition, the Harley-Davidson Financial Services segment faces competition from various banks, insurance companies and other financial institutions that may have access to additional sources of capital at more competitive rates and terms, particularly for borrowers in higher credit tiers.

competitive_position.claim: The LiveWire electric segment is a weak spot. LiveWire Group disclosed substantial doubt about its going concern, and the parent does not plan to fund it beyond the $75.0 million Term Loan.
quotes: In the fourth quarter of 2026, LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its operating income/(loss) guidance.

The Company believes indicators point to a much later EV adoption in the powersports and discretionary leisure industries than the Company originally anticipated given a lack of government incentives and a less favorable regulatory environment, combined with a slower expansion of charging infrastructure.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q balance sheet; the comparison is read directly from the table.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is large against near-term obligations but has fallen since year-end. Cash and cash equivalents were 2,076,378 (table in thousands) at Sep 30, 2026, against 3,091,744 at Dec 31, 2025. Current assets were 4,533,249 against current liabilities of 2,301,069.

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet figures are stated in the 10-Q. The explanation of the debt reduction is from the FY2025 10-K MD&A description of the HDFS Transaction.
financial_health.claim: Debt has been cut sharply over the past year. Long-term debt, net was 1,325,275 (table in thousands) at Sep 30, 2026, against 3,147,836 a year earlier. The current portion of long-term debt was 543,740, against 1,329,244 a year earlier. Total equity was 3,048,762.

The 10-K explains the earlier fall in debt and deposits. It says the tender offer and make-whole redemption on the medium-term notes contributed to a $3.6 billion decrease in HDFS debt and deposits during 2025.
quotes: contributed to the $3.6 billion decrease in HDFS debt and deposits during 2025

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash generation is positive but lower than a year ago. Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months was 275,934 (table in thousands), against 416,903. Capital expenditures were 64,422, against 102,090.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q. The explanation is stated in the 10-Q MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Earnings are a weaker guide to cash than they look. Nine-month net income fell to 144,047 (table in thousands) from 611,709. The prior-year Q3 included a negative credit-loss provision of (301,499) from the release of allowance on receivables sold, a non-cash benefit. Q3 2026 earnings are not boosted this way.
quotes: The benefit realized in the provision for credit losses was driven by the release of the allowance for credit losses for retail finance receivables that were previously being held for investment and were reclassified as held for sale in advance of their sale in the fourth quarter of 2025.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the statements. The mechanism is inferred from the cash flow lines and the FY2025 10-K description.
financial_health.claim: Rebuilding the lending book absorbs cash. In the nine months, origination of finance receivables held for investment was (1,298,341) (table in thousands) against collections of 861,678. Net cash used by investing activities was (417,448), against a 205,477 inflow a year earlier. Non-current finance receivables held for investment rose to 1,142,858 from 719,060 at year-end.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q cash flow statement. The reading that notes were repaid from cash is inferred from zero issuance and the fall in cash.
financial_health.claim: The nine-month cash decline of (998,381) (table in thousands) came mostly from financing outflows. Net cash used by financing activities was (846,378). It included repayments of medium-term notes of (810,950) with no new medium-term note issuance, plus repurchases of common stock of (191,169) and dividends paid of (60,382).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cited items. The tension between them is inferred, and the evidence does not resolve it.
financial_health.claim: Repurchases continued in 2026 even though the company said in February it was pausing discretionary buybacks. The 10-K said the company was pausing them, except for shares due under its ASR program. Cash repurchases were 191,169 (table in thousands) in the nine months, and treasury stock rose to (2,366,374) from (2,111,504). The Q3 release is headed 'Strong Balance Sheet Allowed Continued Capital Return Program'.
quotes: the Company is pausing near-term discretionary share repurchases
Strong Balance Sheet Allowed Continued Capital Return Program

financial_health.basis: Balance sheet classification is stated. How maturities will be met is inferred from the cash, receivables and funding lines. The 2026 notes quote is from the FY2025 10-K.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing needs over the next year are sizeable but sit against a large cash balance. The current portion of long-term debt was 543,740 (table in thousands) and short-term debt was 470,420 at Sep 30, 2026. The FY2025 10-K said part of the ASR/HDFS Transaction proceeds were 'available for settlement of the HDFS medium-term notes due in 2026'.
quotes: with the remainder available for settlement of the HDFS medium-term notes due in 2026

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-Q going-concern and liquidity passage. The going-concern statement is about LiveWire Group, not about Harley-Davidson as a whole.
financial_health.claim: A separate pressure point is LiveWire. LiveWire Group borrowed $75.0 million under its Term Loan on Dec 15, 2025, still outstanding at Sep 30, 2026. LiveWire Group has disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. Harley-Davidson says it does not plan to fund it further beyond that loan and may have to record impairment charges on LiveWire assets.
quotes: In the fourth quarter of 2026, LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its operating income/(loss) guidance.

If its efforts are unsuccessful, the Company may be required to record asset impairment charges related to a portion of its EV assets, primarily certain long-lived assets held in its LiveWire segment.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The base-effect point is inferred from the 10-K retail data.
growth_thesis.claim: Retail demand recovery is the first driver: Q3 2026 worldwide retail sales of new motorcycles rose 5.4% and North America rose 9.1%, while Europe fell 5.3%. For this to continue, North American consumer demand has to keep improving; the 10-Q does not say what supports that demand.
quotes: Worldwide retail sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles in the third quarter of 2026 increased 5.4% compared to the third quarter of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q as management expectation and target.
growth_thesis.claim: A second driver is the Back to the Bricks cost programme. The Company expects cost actions to cut costs by at least $150 million against its 2025 cost base, plus a target of at least an additional $75 million for HDMC, for a total benefit of at least $225 million. This only holds if the cuts are identified and carried out by the end of 2027 without damaging demand.
quotes: The Company expects these cost reduction actions to reduce its costs by at least $150 million compared to its 2025 cost base.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 8-K release and the 10-Q MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Early HDMC margin and expense evidence is mixed. Q3 gross margin rose to 28.1 percent and operating expenses were $227 million, 1 percent lower than a year earlier. HDMC operating income still fell to $44 million, down 18 percent, because shipments, mix and pricing were weaker. Margin gains have to outrun volume, mix and tariff pressure for the cost story to show up in profit.
quotes: Third quarter gross margin percentage increased by 173 bps YoY to 28.1 percent.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as management belief and target; the dependencies come from the risk factor.
growth_thesis.claim: A third driver is the product portfolio: the Sprint and the return of the Sportster are cited as the path to a mid-single-digit retail sales CAGR against 2025. This requires that new products are introduced on time and that the market accepts them.
quotes: including the introduction of the Sprint and return of the Company's iconic Sportster
There is no assurance that the Company will be able to execute its business plans and strategies, including the Company's Back to the Bricks strategic plan.

growth_thesis.basis: Q3 figures are stated in the 8-K; the Q4 and full-year outlook is stated as a management expectation in the 10-Q.
growth_thesis.claim: Dealer inventory discipline lets shipments rise toward retail demand. Global dealer inventory ended Q3 down 26 percent from a year earlier, while Q3 shipments of 33,616 units were down 8 percent. The 2026 shipment and retail outlook is 135,500 to 139,000 units, with Q4 shipments expected above Q4 2025. For this to continue, retail has to keep pace so that restocking does not rest on dealer inventory.
quotes: Global dealer inventory of new motorcycles ended Q3 2026 down 26 percent vs. Q3 2025, and down 6 percent vs Q2 2026.
The Company expects shipments to be higher in the fourth quarter of 2026 as compared to the same quarter in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Q3 figures and receivable balances are stated; the multi-year path is management expectation from the 10-K.
growth_thesis.claim: HDFS is rebuilding on a lower base, which is a recovery driver rather than a current growth driver. Q3 HDFS operating income was $10.8 million, down $428.1 million, after the sale of most of the retail receivables. Non-current finance receivables held for investment rose to 1,142,858 from 719,060 at year-end (table in thousands). Growth depends on continued originations and servicing fees, and on the balance sheet funding them.
quotes: The Company expects HDFS to continue to increase its retail finance receivable base over the coming years as it continues to originate retail finance receivables held for investment.

growth_thesis.claim: Tariff costs are a condition on profit growth. The estimate of gross 2026 tariff cost was raised to a range of $105 million to $120 million. Profit growth requires that tariff costs not rise further, and the Company says it does not expect gross tariff costs to increase in 2027.
quotes: which increased from the Company's previously estimated range of $75 million to $90 million

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts and cash flows are stated; the link to per-share results is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share results have been supported by buybacks, though not by growth in earnings. The Q3 diluted share count was 106,588 against 121,676 a year earlier (in thousands), and nine-month repurchases were 191,169 (table in thousands). Q3 diluted EPS was still $0.40 against $3.10, because the prior year included HDFS one-time benefits. This support continues only if cash generation and capital allocation allow repurchases.
quotes: Strong Balance Sheet Allowed Continued Capital Return Program

material_events.claim: LiveWire Group, Inc., the Company's LiveWire segment entity, disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. The Company says it does not plan to fund LiveWire beyond the existing Term Loan.
quotes: In the fourth quarter of 2026, LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its operating income/(loss) guidance.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q and the 8-K earnings release; the date is the release date, since the 10-Q sentence dates the revisions to October 29, 2026
material_events.claim: LiveWire withdrew its 2026 guidance, and the Company in turn withdrew its own LiveWire guidance.
quotes: As LiveWire Group Inc. withdrew its guidance for 2026, the Company in turn withdrew the guidance it had provided regarding LiveWire.
LiveWire has withdrawn its guidance.

material_events.claim: The Company raised its 2026 outlook for wholesale shipments and worldwide dealer retail sales, and raised HDMC and HDFS guidance.
quotes: Based on the results of the first nine months of 2026, the Company now expects both 2026 wholesale shipments and worldwide dealer retail sales of Harley-Davidson motorcycles of 135,500 to 139,000, which is an increase from the Company's most recent expectation of 133,500 to 138,500 units.
Harley-Davidson Reports Third Quarter Financial Results And Raises HDMC and HDFS Guidance

material_events.claim: The Company announced its new strategic plan, 'Back to the Bricks', which includes cost reduction actions. It is also continuing to review its cost base.
quotes: The Company announced its new strategic plan, called "Back to the Bricks", during the second quarter of 2026.

material_events.claim: The Board added Anthony D. Fassino and Bryan E. Slone as independent directors.
quotes: elected Anthony D. Fassino and Bryan E. Slone to fill the vacancies created by such increase, effective immediately.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A; the 10-Q confirms the sale and the resulting year-over-year decline
material_events.claim: HDFS sold a large part of its retail finance receivables in the HDFS Transaction. This cut HDFS's receivables balance and led the Company to expect lower HDFS operating income.
quotes: HDFS sold $4.1 billion of retail finance receivables originated prior to the HDFS transaction, resulting in the release of the related allowance for credit losses and contributing to a $191.4 million benefit in the provision for credit losses in 2025.

risks.basis: stated in P7; the Q3 loss figures are stated in P5
risks.claim: LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its guidance. The parent says it will not fund it beyond the $75.0 million Term Loan.
quotes: In the fourth quarter of 2026, LiveWire Group, Inc. disclosed conditions and events that raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and withdrew its operating income/(loss) guidance.

risks.basis: stated in P5 and P3; the link to consolidated earnings is inferred from F2
risks.claim: HDFS earnings have shifted to a lower base after the sale of most retail receivables. Q3 HDFS operating income was $10.8 million, down $428.1 million from the prior-year quarter, which held one-time sale benefits.
quotes: The decline was primarily due to the impacts of the sale of the majority of HDFS's retail finance receivables in the prior year quarter to two counterparties, which resulted in a benefit realized in the provision for credit losses and a gain on the sale of securitization beneficial interests.

risks.basis: stated in P5; margin evidence from P8
risks.claim: The tariff cost estimate for the full year was raised. Gross cost is now $105 million to $120 million, up from $75 million to $90 million, and the Company expects no tariff recoveries in 2027.
quotes: Based on the existing tariff environment, the Company does not expect gross tariff costs to increase in 2027 from 2026 nor does the Company expect any tariff recoveries in 2027(1).

risks.basis: stated in P8 and P5; the mechanism is partly inferred from the P5 explanation
risks.claim: HDMC volume and profit are under pressure. Q3 shipments were 33,616 units, down 8 percent. HDMC nine-month operating income was 135,561 against 231,707 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: HDMC global motorcycle shipments of 33,616 units in the quarter were down 8 percent vs. prior year to drive long-term dealer health and in alignment with the Back to the Bricks strategy.

risks.basis: stated in P6 and P5; the counter evidence is stated in P8
risks.claim: Execution of the Back to the Bricks plan is not assured. The plan targets at least $150 million of cost savings plus at least $75 million of HDMC benefit, and it depends on new products and dealer changes.
quotes: There is no assurance that the Company will be able to execute its business plans and strategies, including the Company's Back to the Bricks strategic plan.

risks.basis: inferred from the F1 and F3 balance sheet and cash flow figures
risks.claim: Consolidated cash fell over nine months, from 3,091,744 to 2,076,378 (table in thousands). Operating cash flow was 275,934 against 416,903 a year earlier, and medium-term note repayments and buybacks were large uses of cash.
Collective bargaining agreements at the Company's unionized motorcycle plants expire in October 15, 2027 (Pennsylvania) and March 31, 2029 (Wisconsin), and renewal is not certain.
quotes: The current collective bargaining agreement with hourly employees in Pennsylvania will expire on October 15, 2027, and the agreements with employees in Wisconsin will expire on March 31, 2029.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the 10-Q going-concern passage; the outcome is not stated

quotes: If its efforts are unsuccessful, the Company may be required to record asset impairment charges related to a portion of its EV assets, primarily certain long-lived assets held in its LiveWire segment.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred from the shipment and retail tables and the stated outlook; the realised fourth-quarter result is not in the evidence
unresolved_questions.claim: Will fourth-quarter wholesale shipments rise as guided, after third-quarter shipments of 33,616 units trailed worldwide retail sales of 35,833?
quotes: HDMC global motorcycle shipments of 33,616 units in the quarter were down 8 percent vs. prior year to drive long-term dealer health and in alignment with the Back to the Bricks strategy.
The Company expects shipments to be higher in the fourth quarter of 2026 as compared to the same quarter in 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the 10-Q; the legal outcome is not known
unresolved_questions.claim: How large will full-year 2026 tariff costs and recoveries be, given the gross cost estimate was raised to $105 million to $120 million and tariff legal challenges remain unresolved?
quotes: Certain tariffs have been challenged in U.S. courts, which could impact the continued application of the new or increased tariffs.

unresolved_questions.claim: Will the Back to the Bricks cost savings of at least $150 million, plus an additional $75 million target, show up in expenses, given selling, administrative and engineering expense rose over nine months to 890,672 from 849,098 (table in thousands)?
quotes: The Company expects these cost reduction actions to reduce its costs by at least $150 million compared to its 2025 cost base.

unresolved_questions.basis: inferred; the footnote content is omitted from the item
unresolved_questions.claim: What do the HDMC Adjusted EBITDA adjustments of 13,869 for the quarter and 31,072 for nine months consist of, and will they recur?

unresolved_questions.claim: Where will full-year 2026 HDFS operating income land, given the February range of $45 million to $60 million, nine-month HDFS operating income of 54,595 (table in thousands), and a raised range that is not shown?
